summary: Bosques de las Lomas, Mexico City, Mexico
Dewatering and drying system for chicken manure digestate, 128.7 MT/day at 8% TS
Screw press dewatering, XD-72 rotary drum dryer, biogas conditioning
Basis: Bernardo Urquiza (LETEK) process data of Sep 17 and Oct 13, 2026 and our call of Sep 29, 2026
Validity: 60 days from date of issue · Currency: USD
FOB origin, MCE Stuart, FL or Newkirk, OK shop (per shop load)
intro: Midwest Custom Engineering is pleased to quote Rev C of the budgetary proposal for drying LETEK's chicken manure digestate, sized on the confirmed basis of 128.7 MT/day of liquid digestate at 8% TS, with the grit and sand stream handled separately. Two screw presses dewater the digestate to 30 to 35% TS cake, which drops straight onto the feed screw of an XD-72 rotary drum dryer (7 ft x 35 ft) fired by a 10 MMBtu/hr dual-fuel burner. At 30% TS the drying duty is about 3.6 MMBtu/hr, which your biogas covers with a wide margin; LPG is needed only at start-up or with the digester down. The exhaust passes a stainless cyclone and a 60 HP fan on a VFD, and a biogas conditioning skid is carried as a budget allowance. A reconditioned decanter centrifuge, 304 and 316L stainless drum systems (304 recommended) and a stainless exhaust stack are priced as options. The press line is quoted subject to a test of a sample of your digestate.
design: Liquid digestate › screw press › rotary drum dryer › dried product
Liquid fraction to LETEK treatment (NOM-001); biogas conditioned for the burner
About 34,000 gal/day, 24 h/day, 350 days/year; grit and sand handled separately
Sized at full solids capture; 30 to 35% TS expected from the presses, about 20% from a decanter
About 7.3 to 9.7 MT/day at typical press capture without polymer; polymer raises capture
Rigorous check 3.24; 2.8 at 35% TS cake; 6.3 with the decanter option
Biogas 145.8 MMBtu/day (about 6.1 MMBtu/hr average) covers about 170% of the duty
About 18 bhp at the fan shaft; 60 HP XF-36 fan on a VFD (item 4) also covers the decanter case; drum inlet gas 900 F
liquid: Total N, COD, BOD, total P, oils and grease
liquid_note: Basis: 128.7 MT/day at 8% TS (10.3 MT/day of solids), 30 to 35% TS press cake. Dissolved species (ammonia, chlorides) leave with the water at about the digestate concentration. Total nitrogen will be at least the ammoniacal nitrogen plus the organic nitrogen carried on the uncaptured solids. Polymer raises solids capture and lowers the solids in the liquid. The sample test will firm up these figures; we recommend the same sample be analysed for total N, COD, BOD, total P and oils and grease against the NOM-001 table.

sections.name: Screw Press Dewatering System – 2 Units, Subject to Sample Test
bullets: Two screw presses in parallel, sized for about 35,000 gal/day of digestate at 8% TS, 0.5 mm screen, direct fed by the chopper pump
Chopper feed pump and press drives on VFDs, basic control package; about 50 hp connected for the presses and pumps
Expected cake 30 to 35% TS; lead time about 20 weeks
Stainless steel throughout except the cast iron press bodies, which are kept for rigidity (stainless bodies flex and wear the screens and screws)
Internal protective coating of the press bodies recommended for the chloride and ammonia in this digestate; confirmed and priced after the sample test
Conditional on a test of a sample of your digestate, which confirms cake solids, solids capture and whether polymer is needed
Good mixing ahead of the presses is essential: feed tank and mixer by others, mixer sized after the sample test; polymer make-up system, if needed, quoted after the test

sections.name: XD-72 Mk.2 Rotary Thermal Conditioning System
bullets: Heavy duty direct fired, co-current single pass rotary drum, 7 ft dia x 35 ft long, A36 steel (304 or 316L stainless priced as Options B and C; 304 recommended)
Feed screw with 2 HP motor; the dewatering unit discharges by chute directly onto the feed screw
Heavy duty drop-out box for dry product; airlock with 1.5 HP motor, drive and control devices, mild steel
Drum drive on a structural base with 20 HP motor; full tooth chain sprocket; forged steel drum tracks; front and rear trunnion bases with hardened trunnion wheels and thrust wheel assembly
Front and rear water deluge nozzles for fire suppression; inlet and discharge seals
XF-36 exhaust fan, arrangement #9F, AR 235 rotor, 60 HP TEFC inverter-duty 230-460V/3/60 (VFD, item 4), V-belt drive, 21" inlet, vibration isolation sleeve, inspection door, drain port
Ducting, transitions and elbows up to 60 lineal feet, A36
Basic burner management panel; electrical and control instrumentation for MCE equipment; motor control cabinet, 3 phase, 60 Hz, 480 V
Manual quench nozzles; automated fire suppression quoted on request; the standard burner and valve train are replaced by the dual-fuel burner (item 3)
Commissioning: 1 man-week; installation instructions for the buyer's contractors; start-up and operator training

sections.name: Dual-Fuel Burner Upgrade, 10 MMBtu/hr, LPG + Biogas
bullets: 10 MMBtu/hr maximum with 10:1 turndown; normal fire about 3.6 MMBtu/hr on press cake, with margin for wetter cake, LPG-only operation with the digester down, and the decanter option
Dual-burner system: one LPG burner and one biogas burner, each with stainless combustor sleeve, integral combustion blower and filter, and independent air and gas actuators with position feedback
Two NFPA 86 safety valve trains (LPG and flanged biogas) with dual safety shut-off valves, high and low gas pressure switches and gas meters; automatic changeover to LPG on loss of biogas
Parallel-positioning air/fuel control with separate LPG and biogas fuel profiles, run in the PLC/HMI (item 8)
Burner management panel, NEMA 4X fiberglass enclosure, two self-checking UV flame safeguards, high-temperature limits, combustion E-stop
One week of combustion start-up and tuning on site

sections.name: Exhaust Fan VFD, 60 HP
bullets: Variable frequency drive for the XF-36 exhaust fan: 480 V/3/60, variable-torque rated, NEMA 12 enclosure in the MCC with filtered forced-air cooling
Lockable main breaker, control transformer, door keypad, Ethernet/Modbus link to the PLC
Fan speed trimmed on drum outlet draft, so the exhaust airflow follows the drying load and can be capped at the cyclone maximum in the decanter case
Programming included in item 8

sections.name: HE-36 Cyclone
bullets: Dryer exhaust collector, budget selection for 6,342 ACFM at 230 F (HE-36 operating range 6,175 to 7,600 CFM)
Final cyclone picked with MCE's cyclone sizing calculator after the sample test, once cake solids and solids capture, and so the exhaust flow, are confirmed
36 in diameter, 25.5 x 10.75 in tangential inlet, 10 in flanged discharge, mount pads and inspection port; fines rejoin the dried product

sections.name: HE-36 Cyclone – 304 Stainless Construction Adder
bullets: 304 stainless construction of the cyclone for the wet, ammonia-laden dryer exhaust

sections.name: FT-12 Airlock
bullets: Rotary airlock under the cyclone discharge; fines rejoin the dried product

sections.name: Automation and Controls (PLC / HMI)
bullets: Required with the dual-fuel burner: the PLC hosts the parallel-positioning fuel profiles for LPG and biogas and the automatic changeover logic
PLC programming of infeed, outfeed and product conveyance, burner modulation (BMS) and dryer temperature control; links to the dewatering unit, fan VFD, biogas skid and plant system
21.5" HMI with modeled equipment interface, data logging of temperatures and component hours, visualization, e-mailed PDF reports and mobile data access
On-site programming for 1 man-week; additional days at $1,350/day plus expenses

sections.name: Biogas Conditioning Skid, 500 ppm Inlet – Budget Allowance
bullets: For 195 scfm (7,455 Nm3/day) of biogas at 500 ppm H2S or less (bulk H2S removal in the digester by others)
Iron-oxide polishing vessels to under 100 ppm, gas cooler and moisture knockout, booster blower to 2 psig
Inlet and outlet flame arresters, pressure control, inlet and outlet gas analyzers (CH4, H2S, O2)
Local control panel linked to the burner BMS; first charge of iron-oxide media; process design MCE-LETEK-BGS-001
Budget allowance from our component estimate for this design (accuracy about +/-30%); firmed up into a fixed price once the biogas analysis is available

options.name: Reconditioned Decanter Centrifuge, in lieu of the screw presses (item 1)
bullets: If the sample test shows the solids are too fine for a screw press
Includes the cyclone step-up to an HE-47 in 304 stainless for the higher airflow (HE-47 range 10,825 to 12,600 CFM)
Cake about 20% TS instead of 30 to 35%: dryer duty about 6.3 MMBtu/hr (biogas covers about 96%, the rest LPG) and exhaust about 11,200 ACFM; polymer is more likely to be needed
Availability and lead time confirmed when a specific reconditioned unit is selected

options.name: RECOMMENDED: 304 Stainless Steel Drum System, in lieu of the A36 drum system (item 2)
bullets: 304 stainless drum shell and flights, feed screw, drop-out box and airlock in place of A36
Our recommended balance of cost and service life for this digestate (ammonia, chlorides, pH about 8); estimated shell life of 3/8 in A36 on this service is 7 to 10 years
Stainless pricing subject to mill prices at order

options.name: 316L Stainless Steel Drum System, in lieu of the A36 drum system (item 2) – alternative to Option B
bullets: Same scope as Option B, in 316L: the molybdenum gives better resistance to chloride pitting (about 3,000 mg/L chlorides in this digestate)
$64,500 more than Option B; stainless pricing subject to mill prices at order

Fan outlet transition and side-inlet tee; base stand with base plate and condensate drain; open vertical discharge
Two 4 in sampling ports at 90 degrees located to EPA Method 1, plus a thermocouple port; guy ring with three guy wires and turnbuckles; stainless bolting
Sized for both the press and decanter cases (about 2,100 to 3,700 fpm exit velocity); foundation, anchors, sampling platform and ladder, and installation by others
